articleTitle: Design and Development of an Internet of Things (IoT)-Based Application and System to Detect Stunting in Infants and Toddlers
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Currently, the process of monitoring children’s growth in Indonesia relies on manual methods for collecting anthropometric data. These methods pose a risk of data recording errors. Additionally, the ratio of healthcare workers to children in Indonesia is 1:90, a significant disparity that hinders efforts to reduce the prevalence of stunting in the country. To support the third Sustainable Development Goal (SDG), which emphasizes “Good Health and Well-being,” it is crucial to address issues in the stunting management process, from data collection to monitoring. The design and development of this iOS-based mobile application aim to assist in monitoring child growth and provide guidance and steps for prevention and treatment. Besides application development, it also involves the design and development of an Internet of Things (IoT) system to aid in the collection of children’s anthropometric data. The research methodology includes studying stunting cases in Indonesia, anthropometric data calculation methods, stunting prevention and management steps, application design and development, automatic anthropometric data collection, and online data storage and transmission using IoT technology. The developed application and system have been tested and successfully integrated. The IoT device has an accuracy rate of 99.83% for weight measurement calibration and 98.68% for height or length measurement calibration. From the testing results of the child condition calculation method in the application, an accuracy rate of 100% was achieved.

articleTitle: Identifying User Personas of Indonesian Professional Workers Who Activate Dark Mode UI: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: This study investigates the personalization preferences of Indonesian working professionals, specifically focusing on the adoption of Dark Mode. By conducting an online survey and employing K-Means clustering with Silhouette Score evaluation, three distinct user personas were identified: Millennials, Older Millennials and Generation X, and Younger Millennials and Generation Z. All user personas have different motivation in activating Dark Mode. Older Millennials and Generation X are primarily motivated to activate Dark Mode UI to conserve battery life, particularly when using chat applications. In contrast, younger Millennials and Generation Z are driven by both comfort and power-saving considerations, especially while engaging with social media and chat applications. Millennials activate Dark Mode across various digital platforms, including e-commerce, social media, chat services, and entertainment. Despite demographic and device usage differences, a commonality among these groups was their frequent use of chat applications. The findings indicate that chat applications are particularly popular among Dark Mode users and suggest that implementing Dark Mode as a UI option can enhance user engagement and retention within these platforms.

articleTitle: Development of a Mobile Monitoring Application for a Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT)-Based Struvite Fertilizer Production System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Struvite fertilizer, characterized by its slow-release qualities, is comprised of magnesium, ammonium, and phosphate and is vital for plant growth. The Integrated Laboratory Unit of Universitas Syiah Kuala (USK) has developed a prototype for struvite fertilizer production equipment, but the production process requires manual monitoring. This project seeks to create an MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport)-based mobile application for the real-time monitoring and control of struvite fertilizer production equipment. The application employs the MQTT communication protocol, known for its quick data transmission and minimal bandwidth requirements. This application incorporates sensors on the production machine, which includes a reactor, filter, and dryer, and employs an Amazon Web Service’s (AWS) IoT Core as the MQTT broker. Findings from the application’s evaluation indicate that the mobile application can efficiently monitor and control several machine components. Data transmission to MQTT topics was successful, facilitating seamless communication. Functional and integration testing demonstrated that the system operates effectively. Usability testing outcomes yielded an average score of 77.75 with a system usability scale (SUS) approach, signifying that the application possesses a satisfactory degree of usability classified within the “Grade B” category.

articleTitle: Evaluating a User Interface for M-Commerce Shoe Sales
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Interface engineering maximizes user experience by defining the form, function, and interfaces utility. Current interfaces have not optimized user-system interaction. This study aimed to develop a compatible and user-friendly interface to improve user efficiency. Android Studio was used to create a simple and functional interface. The commands combination was designed to prioritize simplicity, reducing user stress. Continuous evaluations support to identify areas for improvement and optimize the interface’s performance. The results exposed the application developed was well-received, providing a simple and effective interface. Users reported better interaction and superior satisfaction with the system, confirming the proposed design effectiveness. The user interface developed, currently maximizes the experience, with a user rating of 75% indicating that design is simple and functional. Continuous evaluation and improvement guarantee that application will evolve to fulfill more complex future needs, contributing to user well-being and efficiency.

articleTitle: Empowering MSMEs in Indonesia: A Mobile Application for Digital Transformation and Sustainable Economic Growth Post-COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Titled Empowering MSMEs in Indonesia: A Mobile Application for Digital Transformation and Sustainable Economic Growth Post-COVID-19 this study highlights the challenges faced by MSMEs in Indonesia due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on data from the Ministry of Cooperatives and MSMEs, the number of MSMEs in Indonesia in 2022 will reach more than 64 million, but the majority have experienced a drastic decline in revenue. With only around 19 million MSMEs doing business online, there is an urgent need to improve digital literacy and access to business resources. We propose the development of a mobile application that not only provides digital marketing training, but also facilitates MSMEs in accessing a network of influencers and content creators. The app is designed to accelerate the digital transformation of MSMEs, expand market reach, and support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals 8, namely decent work and economic growth. Through this solution, we hope to encourage inclusive and sustainable economic growth in Indonesia.

articleTitle: UX Analysis of Augmented Reality in E-Commerce Marketing Using the System Usability Scale and Usability Testing Method
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Changes in consumer behavior from offline to online shopping have forced business owners to develop their product marketing through e-commerce. One of the technologies used to support this marketing process is AR (Augmented Reality). AR technology provides an interesting shopping experience for its users. However, the inconsistency of AR results and the unfamiliarity of AR among consumers have made this feature not widely used. Therefore, to find out what improvements can be made, it is necessary to evaluate the user experience. This research focuses on analyzing user experience on AR in e-commerce (Shopee) using two methods, System Usability Scale and Usability Testing. The number of respondents for the analysis with the SUS method was 100 respondents and for the Usability Testing method was 10 respondents. The final score obtained from the SUS calculation was 64.45, while the Usability Testing method obtained: learnability of 100%, efficiency of 71%, memorability 4, and error of 0.13. The results of this study can provide improvements to the AR feature UI for the company that provide AR for new feature and provide additional knowledge for academics which is by combining 2 methodologies can provide a better analysis of the use of AR in product marketing.

articleTitle: User Experience Evaluation on Siakadcloud’s Computer Based Test Front (CBTFRONT) Application Using Evaluation of Heuristic Method
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The rapid development of information systems technology is not only limited to the transformation of data into information but can also improve the efficiency and effectiveness of an organization’s performance, especially in the world of education. PT SEVIMA is presented as a consultant and developer of information systems technology that created the Computer Based Test Front (CBTFront) siAkadCloud application, a system designed to optimize the exam process and reduce cheating during the exam. Since the application was released in 2019 until now, there has never been tested for user experience evaluation. Thus, The research objective is to use a heuristic evaluation method to identify user experience through the application. The results of the evaluation before improvement had 8 heuristic problems with an average severity rating of 2.5 out of 4 based on the severity rating scale, which means it is important to make improvements and become a top priority. Improvements add a Single Sign-On (SSO) system, add titles to each description and provide more informative exam details, change the layout and change the wording on the button and add a proctoring feature. After improvement in the form of the prototype design, the average severity ratings were reduced to 0.2 out of 4 based on severity rating scale, which means there are no problems at all with its use. The results of the improvements that have been made have proven to fulfil the 10 principles of heuristic evaluation.

articleTitle: Improving Programmer Work Quality with ChatGPT Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The potential of artificial intelligence as a tool that can be an assistant for humans is very close. This is reinforced by the breakthrough of a generative model that is considered to be able to help many tasks that are usually done by humans, namely ChatGPT. ChatGPT successfully demonstrated its potential by providing complete and intact code generation. ChatGPT, with GPT-3, is one of many language models currently available for people. In previous research, ChatGPT was tested to see if it could provide appropriate programming code results and perform large-scale data analysis on a specific dataset described in sentence form. The limitations of ChatGPT include understanding and generating code, which requires further training data. This opportunity positions ChatGPT as a provider of programming materials and a place to seek solutions to problems faced by programmers. This paper investigates the capabilities and also limitations of ChatGPT to help with the works of programmer’s daily tasks by examining overall ChatGPT capabilities within the assigned environment as a Programmer Assistant and examining the overall probability of ChatGPT limitations and failures to generate the results from specified prompts from the programmer. This study formulated the research question and performed the PRISMA step to answer the question. This study found significant potential for ChatGPT as a programmer’s assistant, catering to requests related to programming and design, and also functions as a tool for designing programming code to be implemented in software development.

articleTitle: A Foresight Course Framework for Undergraduates Designing Human-Centric Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The growing complexity of global challenges that advocate human values necessitates a shift towards future oriented, human-centric design approaches. Such thinking is embedded in a foresight-driven coursework, part of the Bachelor of Information Technology (Hons) offered in Universiti Teknologi MARA. It trains students to anticipate future trends and co-create innovative, resilient and sustainable solutions. In this paper we elaborate how foresight methodology, when integrated with participatory design approach, can result in powerful human-centric solutions that are future-proof. Through future tools such as horizon scanning, the seven questions technique, issues paper, driver mapping, futures wheel, SWOT analysis, prototyping and road mapping, students engage with stakeholder to address present and future challenges, equipping them to design adaptable, human-centric technological solutions.

articleTitle: User Interface and User Experience Optimization in E-commerce: Exploring Factors to Increase Purchase Intention
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: In today’s digital era, e-commerce has become a crucial part of global retail, changing how consumers shop, and businesses operate. The convenience and accessibility of online shopping have made e-commerce platforms the preferred choice for millions of consumers worldwide. However, the success of these platforms depends on more than just product availability; it is deeply tied to the seamless integration of user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) design. Nearly 60% of e-commerce users abandon their shopping carts without completing their purchases, a problem caused by various factors, including user experience. Previous research has indicated that positive user experiences can increase society’s willingness to make purchases. This article, which employs a qualitative descriptive approach along with a systematic literature review (SLR) methodology, aims to identify the key factors influencing UI and UX in e-commerce and their impact on consumers’ purchase intentions. The information extracted from each study includes the researcher’s background, problem, research gap, the purpose of the study, methodologies, research sector, country of publication, interviewee size, research model, framework, data analysis methods, variables tested, hypothesis test findings, research limitations, suggestions for future research, and recommended measures. The findings from this SLR highlight the complex nature of optimizing UI and UX in e-commerce to boost purchase intention. Ergonomics ensures the platform is user-friendly and intuitive, quality builds trust by maintaining high service and information standards, and user preference creates a personalized and engaging experience.

articleTitle: Applying Design Thinking in User Interface Design: A Case Study of Primakara University International Office
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The International Office plays a critical role in higher education by managing international programs such as student recruitment, exchanges, and research collaborations, which are essential for enhancing a university’s global presence and reputation. Recognizing this, Primakara University sought to design a dedicated International Office website to improve its competitiveness and educational quality on an international level. This website serves as a vital tool for communicating with international audiences and promoting inclusive educational opportunities. The user interface design process employed the Design Thinking method, which facilitates a deep understanding of user needs through iterative stages of problem definition, ideation, prototyping, and testing. The final testing phase, conducted using the User Experience Questionnaire Plus (UEQ+), indicated a generally positive user experience, with an overall average score of 2.09 across 15 scales. While Dependability, Efficiency, Stimulation, and Trust scored slightly lower, the quality of content achieved the highest rating, demonstrating the website’s effectiveness in making a favorable impression on users.

articleTitle: A Modified Usefulness, Satisfaction, and Ease-of-Use Questionnaire for Pre-Elderly Users)
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Interactive system design and development always involves testing and evaluation to ensure that user needs and expectations are met, including the pre-elderly (aged 45–59) population who have unique emotional and functional requirements compared to other categories of users. However, the existing evaluation methods still fall short in addressing this demographic’s needs and preferences. In order to properly address the challenges faced by pre-elderly users, this study proposes a modified method of evaluating the usability aspects of application of the existing USE (Usefulness, Satisfaction, and Ease-of-Use) questionnaire. The questionnaire was modified by paraphrasing and removing certain questions, while also incorporating user interface as a new specific key factor. The modification resulted in 18 items within five factors. A sample of 62 pre-elderly users participated in completing the modified questionnaire after finishing structured mobile news app scenario testing. The factor analysis results demonstrate that the modified questionnaire effectively captures both functional and non-functional requirements specific to pre-elderly users. While all 18 items were retained, they were categorized into two distinct factors: Ease of Use and Learning, and User Interface and Satisfaction. The findings of this study are anticipated to contribute to future research on user experience evaluation tools that are more tailored to the specific needs of pre-elderly users. Furthermore, these findings offer invaluable insights for enhancing the usability and user experience of mobile news applications, thereby improving user satisfaction and engagement.

articleTitle: The Continuous Use of a Highway Traffic Management System (HTMS) Services on Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Mobile applications are used across various fields and for different purposes. M-commerce, social media, education, and navigation are just a few examples of applications available on mobile platforms. These applications enable users to access them anytime and anywhere. However, there is a limited number of mobile applications that specifically provide information about traffic, emergency services (SOS), toll fares, amenities, and more. As one of the largest highway concessionaires in Malaysia, XYZ has also developed a mobile application to disseminate information to highway users. Thus, the purpose of this study is to examine the factors that influence the continued use of the XYZ mobile application. The results show that user experience factors—such as Effort Use (EU), Social Influence (SI), Accuracy (ACC), Completeness (COM), Pragmatic Quality (PQ), Stimulation Quality (SQ), Identity Quality (IQ), and Attractiveness (ATT)—positively affect the continued use of the XYZ mobile application.

articleTitle: Interacting with Automated Vehicles: Effects of Trait Driving Anger and Time Gaps
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: Automated vehicles (AVs) are being deployed in public traffic, which brings not only potential improvements in safety and efficiency but also new challenges for human drivers. This study investigates the effect of trait driving anger and varying time gaps between AVs and human-driven vehicles (HVs) in terms of drivers’ driving performance and level of arousal. Thirty-four participants engaged in a simulated driving experiment, which involved following AVs with different time gaps: free drive (infinite gap), medium time gap (5 seconds), and small time gap (1 second). Driving performance was measured using a combination of longitudinal and lateral control metrics, while physiological arousal was assessed using heart rate variability (HRV) and skin conductance level (SCL). The results indicated that small time gaps impair driving performance and increase arousal levels when compared with the free drive condition. The interaction of medium time gaps and high trait driving anger was negatively associated with the human driver’s level of arousal, which suggested a potential to mitigate the driving anger with an appropriate time gap. These findings highlight the need to consider the impact of trait driving anger and time gap settings in mixed traffic environments involving AVs.

articleTitle: Analysing the Impact of Rhythm Game in Enhancing Typing Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The research was centered on adapting and assessing a new, unique game concept. The game onKeys presents a new approach and poses as an alternative method for improving typing skills. However, despite offering a promising avenue, the game still grapples with certain limitations. Utilizing the MDA Framework, the study seeks to integrate additional game components into onKeys and evaluate its effectiveness in improving typing skills. A paired T-test is used to assess the Pre-Test and Post-Test data. The System Usability Scale gathers subjective feedback about the game design’s usability. This study found that the onKeys game has little impact on players’ typing speed and accuracy, which may be attributed to a higher average typing speed, short period of playtime or a small sample size. However, upon reviewing the record and survey data, particularly the System Usability Score, it becomes evident that the game design still has potential. Further research can delve deeper into this game concept and design.

articleTitle: Indonesian Language Learning Application as the Key to Equalizing Educational Development in Indonesia, Especially in Remote, Outermost, and Underdeveloped Areas (3T)
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The term 3T refers to regions categorized as remote, outermost, and underdeveloped (terluar, terdepan, tertinggal) in Indonesia, which lags in development compared to the other areas nationally. This study aims to explore the technological possibilities applicable in 3T areas for the process of learning the Indonesian language. This study also seeks to identify the user experience design process and the testing outcomes of a mobile application for learning Indonesian, which incorporates gamification and artificial intelligence translation. This research uses the Design Thinking methodology for designing the prototype and utilizes SEQ (Single Ease Question) and SUS (System Usability Scale) for the testing results. The SEQ task completion results show an average score of 6.03, indicating that the prototype is categorized as easy to use. Additionally, the SUS score results show a value of 78.33, indicating that the usability of the BIINDO prototype is acceptable, nearing the level between good and excellent.

articleTitle: The Learning Outcomes Achievement and User Experience Analysis of a Cryptography Education Web Game
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: The rising threat of cybercrimes in Indonesia, including a significant breach of the national data center, reveals the urgent need for effective cybersecurity education. Cryptography, a key component of cybersecurity, is often difficult for beginners to grasp. To address this, we developed an interactive web game that blends puzzle-solving with a visual novel to make cryptographic concepts more accessible. This study analyzes the game’s user experience (UX) using the ARCS model—Attention, Relevance, Confidence, Satisfaction—and assesses learning outcomes by comparing pre-test and post-test results. The findings show significant improvements in participants’ understanding and high levels of engagement, demonstrating a strong correlation between positive user experience and enhanced learning outcomes. However, some aspects of the educational content still need refinement. Future updates will offer multilingual support and personalized learning paths, with pre-and post-tests targeting specific cryptography and cybersecurity sub concepts, and analysis of UX features through targeted surveys and in-game analytics to enhance learning experiences.

articleTitle: Identifying User-Desirable Centralized Scholarship Information System Features: A Survey Among Indonesian Scholarship Seekers
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International HCI and UX Conference in Indonesia (CHIuXiD)
abstract: A scholarship could improve the life quality of a person with limited resources. However, the information about the offers was often scattered among the internet and made it difficult to meet the needs of scholarship seekers. Furthermore, the government and private sector who provide the grants also have difficulty finding the best applicants. There are only a few studies about building a centralized scholarship information system based on the user experience. The main goal of this study is to enhance the centralized scholarship information systems user experience by offering a set of features that the user needs. We carried out literature reviews and administered a survey to 204 individuals throughout Indonesia. We identified the needs for 7 key features, which are listed as prioritized through weighted scoring: scholarship selection preparation study features, List of All Scholarships by Level, Discussion Forum with Fellow Awardees, Comparison Table Between Scholarship Programs, Scholarship Program Opening Notification & Registration Progress Recommendations for Scholarship Programs That Suit User Needs, Mentor Assistance/Consultation Session. We also found 6 additional features that are mentioned by some respondents that are considerable: articles, community, information about scholarship destination countries, competition maps, templates, and preparation checks. Our findings have the potential to assist researchers and practitioners in enhancing the user experience during the development of a centralized scholarship information system.
